name: Maganettawan
location: On the River Maganettawan.
remarks: Reserved under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty, 9th September, 1850; subsequently surveyed and confirmed by O.C., 31st January, 1853.

name: Henvey Inlet
location: At Henvey Inlet on Georgian Bay.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Point Grondin
location: At Point Grondin, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: White Fish River
location: At the mouth of White Fish River, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Spanish River
location: At the mouth of Spanish River, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: White Fish River
location: At White Fish Lake, about 16 miles north of Collins Inlet, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve was not surveyed until 1884. The boundaries as then surveyed were amended and established by judgement of the court of 21st January, 1889. (Attorney General of Ontario vs. Francis et al.)

name: Serpent River
location: The peninsula east of the mouth of Serpent River, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Mississagua River
location: At the mouth of Mississagua River, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Dokis
location: On French River.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Nipissing
location: On the north shore of Lake Nipissing.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Wanapitae
location: At Lake Wanapitae.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Thessalon
location: At the south-east corner of the Township of Thessalon, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve originally consisted of the entire township, all of which, except the present reserve, has been surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians. (See note to No. 1.)

name: French River
location: At Ogawaning on French River.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Garden River
location: At Garden River, near Sault Ste. Marie.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve originally consisted of a tract containing about 130,000 acres, all of which, except the present reserve, has been surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Goulais Bay
location: At Batchewaung Bay, east end of Lake Superior; includes a small island situated at Sault Ste. Marie.
remarks: The whole of the original reserve, excepting the island at Sault Ste. Marie, which contained about 157,440 acres, was set apart under the Robinson Huron Treaty, subsequently surveyed and finally confirmed by O.C., 31st January, 1852. It was surrendered for sale, for the benefit of the Indians, in 1859. The present reserve at Goulais Bay is a portion of the original reserve set apart by Orders in Council in 1879 and 1885. The island at Sault Ste. Marie has never been surrendered.

name: Parry Island
location: In Georgian Bay, near its eastern shore
remarks: Under the provisions of the Robinson-Huron Treaty the reserve was located on the mainland. The island was surveyed in lieu of that location, and the survey approved by the Commissioner of Crown Lands, 22nd November, 1853.

name: Shawanaga
location: In the Township of Shawanaga, Parry Sound District.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Naiscoutaing
location: In the Township of Wallbridge and Harrison, Parry Sound District.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

location: Lots 34 and 35, concession 7, Township of Shawanaga, Parry Sound District.
remarks: Vested by Order in Council of the Provincial Government dated 31st December, 1877, in the Dominion Government in trust for the Shawanga Band of Indians so long as the said band continues to occupy the said lots.

name: Temogaming
location: At Lake Temogaming
tribe_band: A band of Ojibbewas of Lake Huron, who had not been provided with a reserve under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty.
remarks: Surveyed in 1884. The reserve has not been confirmed by the Provincial Government of Ontario.

name: Cockburn Island
location: On Cockburn Island, Lake Huron.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: The Manitoulin Islands and islands on the north shore of Lake Huron were set apart, 9th August, 1836, by Sir Edmund Head, as a reserve for the Ottawas and Chippewas, and any other Indians who should be allowed to settle thereon. The Manitoulin and adjacent islands were surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians 6th October, 1862, and under the provisions of this surrender the present reserves, numbered 19 to 26 inclusive, were set apart.

name: Sheshewaning
location: Manitoulin Island.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Obidgewong
location: Manitoulin Island.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: West Bay
location: Manitoulin Island.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sucker Creek
location: Manitoulin Island.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sheguiandah
location: Manitoulin Island.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sucker Lake
location: Manitoulin Island.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Manitoulin Island (unceded portion)
location: The eastern peninsula of Manitoulin Island.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Cape Croker
location: Saugeen Peninsula
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: The Saugeen Peninsula was set apart as an Indian reserve 9th August, 1836, by Sir Edmund Head, and surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians 13th October, 1854. Reserves Nos. 27, 28 and 29 were set apart under the provisions of the said surrender of 13th October, 1854.

name: Chief's Point.
location: Saugeen Peninsula
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Saugeen Reserve
location: At the south-western corner of the Saugeen Peninsula.
tribe_band: Ottawa and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Christian Islands, viz.: - Christian, Hope and Beckwith.
location: In Lake Huron
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lake Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron.
remarks: These islands were reserved in the surrender made by these Indians, 5th June, 1856, of the islands situated in Lake Huron which they claimed. The islands in Lake Huron claimed by these Indians were ceded in error in 1850 by the Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Gibson
location: The eastern portion of the Township of Gibson, County of Muskoka.
remarks: Purchased from the Provincial Government in 1881 for such members of the Oka Band of Indians as might desire to settle there.

name: Rama
location: In township of Rama, County of Ontario.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lakes Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron
remarks: Purchased from private parties at different dates between 1843 and 1848.

name: Georgina Island
location: Georgina and Snake Islands in Lake Simcoe, and other islands in Lake Couchiching.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lakes Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron
remarks: These islands have remained in the possession of the Indians, and have never been ceded by them by treaty or purchase.

name: Scugog
location: On the Island in Lake Scugog.
remarks: Purchased by these Indians with the proceeds of their own annuities, 3rd Nov., 1843.

name: Mud Lake
location: On Mud Lake, in the Township of Smith, County of Peterborough.
remarks: Granted in 1837 to the New England Company. Transferred to the Dominion Government in trust for the Indians 12th Oct., 1898

name: Rice Lake
location: On the north shore of Rice Lake, in the County of Peterborough.
tribe_band: Mississaguas of Rice, Mud and Scugog Lakes.
remarks: 1,120 acres of this reserve was granted in 1834 to trustees for the benefit of Indian tribes in the Province. The remainder of the reserve was purchased by the Indians with their own funds.

name: Islands in the Trent water
location: In the Counties of Peterborough and Victoria.
tribe_band: Mississaguas of Rice, Mud and Scugog Lakes.
remarks: Claimed by these Indians not to have been included in treaty of 1818, and claim subsequently admitted by the Crown Lands Department.

name: Alnwick
location: In the Township of Alnwick, County of Northumberland.
remarks: Purchased from private owners at different dates between 1836 and 1870.

name: Tyendinaga
location: On the Bay of Quinté - The southern part of the Township of Tyendinaga.
tribe_band: Mohawks of the Bay of Quinté
remarks: The reserve consisted originally of 92,700 acres granted under letters patent from the Crown in 1793, all of which except the present reserve has been surrendered and sold and the proceeds applied for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Golden Lake
location: At the southern end of Golden Lake, in the County of Peterborough.
remarks: Purchased by the Dominion Government from the Provincial Government of Ontario in 1870 as a reserve for these Indians.

name: Tuscarora
location: The township of Tuscarora and parts of the Township of Oneida's and Onondaga.
tribe_band: The Six Nations, consisting of the Mohawks, Oneidas, Onondagas, Tuscaroras, Cayugas, Senecas and Delawares
remarks: A tract six miles wide on each side of the Grand River was granted to the Six Nations in 1784 by Sir F. Haldimand containing about 694,910 acres. This grant was confirmed to them by Letters Patent in 1793 by Governor Simcoe. All of the tract except the present reserve has been surrendered in portions from time to time and sold for the benefit of the Indians. In 1847 the Six Nations invited the Mississaguas of the Credit to settle on their reserve, and offered them a free grant of 6,000 acres for the purpose. A number accepted, who now reside in the south-west corner of the reserve.

name: Oneida
location: In the Township of Delaware, County of Middlesex.
remarks: Purchased for these Indians by the Government in 1840 with their own money which they brought with them from the United States.

name: Caradoc
location: In the Township of Caradoc, County of Middlesex.
tribe_band: Chippewas of the Thames and Munsees.
remarks: Reserved by the Chippewas in the cession made by them of the 'Longwood Tract' in 1819. A small portion of the reservation was surrendered in 1834 and sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Stony Point
location: In the Township of Bosanquet, County of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail, Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western Districts made by them in 1827.

name: Kettle Point
location: In the Township of Bosanquet, County of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail, Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western Districts made by them in 1827.

name: Sarnia
location: In the Township of Sarnia, County of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail, Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western Districts made by them in 1827.

name: Walpole Island
location: At the head of Lake St. Clair
tribe_band: Chippewas and Pottawattamies of Walpole Island.
remarks: The Chippewas settled on the Island in 1831 by order of the Government. The island appears to have been then set apart by the Government as Crown Reserve to be used for the purpose of settling Indians thereon. The Potawattamies came from the United States in 1841 and on petition were permitted by the Government to settle on the island.

name: Orford
location: In the Township of Orford, County of Kent.
remarks: The reserve originally consisted of 51,160 acres situated in the Townships of Zone and Orford and was set apart by Order in Council in 1798. All the reservation except the present reserve has been surrendered and sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Michipicoten
location: On the Michipicoten River, about one mile from its mouth.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. This reserve has not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Gros Cap
location: On the north shore of Lake Superior, about a mile west of Michipicoten River.
remarks: Set apart in accordance with the provisions of the Robinson Superior Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Pic River
location: On the Pic River, near its mouth.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Paps Plat
location: At Pays Plat, north of Lake Superior.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Fort William
location: Near the west end of Lake Superior.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Superior Treaty. (See note No. 1.)

name: Red Rock
location: On Nepigon River.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: McIntyre Bay
location: On the south shore of Lake Nepigon.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians of Lake Nepigon. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Gull River
location: At the mouth of Gull River on the west shore of Lake Nepigon.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Superior Treaty. Surveyed in 1887. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Island Point
location: On the west shore of Lake Nepigon.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians of Lake Nepigon. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Jackfish Island
location: A small island near the west shore of Lake Nepigon.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians of Lake Nepigon. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Long Lake
location: At the north end of Long Lake.
remarks: Surveyed in 1886 for the Indians residing on the land. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Cornwall Island
location: In the River St. Lawrence near the boundary between Ontario and Quebec.
remarks: This and adjacent islands form part of the reserve of these Indians held by them from the time the time French rule began in this country.

name: Saugeen Indians Hunting Ground.
location: Lots 11 to 20 inclusive in Cons. III and IV, lots 11 to 18 and lot 20 in Cons. I and II, all east of the Road, Township of St. Edmund, County of Bruce.
tribe_band: Saugeen and Cape Bury Croker Bands.
remarks: Set apart by Order in Council of 16th November, 1896. Lots 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 20 in Cons. I and II, E.B.R., are set apart for the Saugeen Reserve Indians, and lots 11 to 20 inclusive in Cons. III and IV, E.B.R., for the Cape Croker Band.

name: Restigouche
location: At the mouth of the Restigouche River, adjacent to the west boundary of the Township of Mann, County of Bonaventure.
remarks: This reserve is a portion of the area of land set apart and appropriated under the Statute 14 and 15, Victoria, Chapter 106, for the benefit of the Indian tribes in Lower Canada. The total area of land set apart by the Statute amounted to 230,000 acres.

name: Maria
location: At the mouth of the Grand Cascapedia River, in the Township of Maria, County of Bonaventure.
remarks: Settled on and claimed by the Indians from time immemorial.

name: Betsiamits
location: At the mouth of the Betsiamits River, on the north shore of the St. Lawrence River, in the County of Saguenay.
tribe_band: Montagnais, Tadousacs, Papinachois, Nauthapi and other Nomadic tribes.
remarks: A portion of the area set apart under the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Ouiatchouan
location: On the west shore of Lake St. John, in the County of Chicoutimi.
tribe_band: Montagnais of Lake St. John and Tadousac.
remarks: Originally consisted of the entire township, containing 23,000 acres, set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. The whole township, with the exception of the present reserve has been surrendered, and is being sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Lorette
location: In the County of Quebec, about eight miles from the city.
remarks: This village, which is said to have contained an area of 40 arpents, set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. The whole township, with the exception of the present reserve has been surrendered, and is being sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Quarante Arpents
location: In the County of Quebec, about three miles from Lorette.
remarks: Gift from the Jesuit Fathers, dated 7th March, 1842, and again confirmed in the deed of gift of the 26th February, 1794, mentioned above.

name: Rocmont
location: In the Township of Rocmont, County of Portneuf.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No.1.)

name: Crespieul
location: West of the Township of Crespieul, in the County of St. John.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No.1.)

name: Becancour
location: Near Becancour in the County of Nicolet. The reserve consists of lot No. 582, in the Concession du Village Sauvage, and Islands Nos. 574, 488 and 489, in the Becancour River.
remarks: These Indians were once the proprietors of the Seigniory of Becancour, granted to them 30th April, 1708. In 1760 they sold the whole of their territory except the lot and islands which now constitute their reserve.

name: Pierreville
location: At Pierreville in the County of Yamaska. Consists of the following lands, situated in the Seigniories of Pierreville and St. Francis du Lac, viz.:
remarks: Two large grants of land in Pierreville and St. Francis were made in 1700 and 1701, to these Indians by private parties. The present reserve is all they now possess, the whole of the remainder having been leased or otherwise conceded to whites.

name: 1218 2nd Con. St. Jacques or No. 1 on the especial plan
1219 3rd Con St. Jacques or No. 24 on the especial plan
850 A small Island lying between Atcombac and Au Pin Island
482 3rd Con. Parish of St. Francis or No. 41 on the especial plan
972 A lot in the Village of Pierreville
Caughnawaga
location: On the south bank of the St. Lawrence River, in the County of Laprairie.
remarks: Part of a grant made in 1680 to the Jesuits for the conversion, instruction and subsistence of the Iroquois. The title was vested in the Iroquois under the supervision of the Indian Department, 15th April, 1762, by judgment of Military Council assembled at Montreal.

name: St. Regis
location: On the south bank of the St. Lawrence River, in the Township of Dundee, County of Huntingdon.
remarks: This reserve is a part of the hunting grounds of the Iroquois, which were in their possession at the time of the French rule in this country.

name: The reserve consists of the following lands, viz.:
Islands in the St. Lawrence reported on by agent John Davidson, not included in the Cadastral list
Doncaster
location: The southerly portion of the Township of Doncaster, in the County of Montcalm.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No. 1)

name: Maniwaki
location: At the confluence of the Desert River with the Gatineau River, in the County of Ottawa
tribe_band: Algonquins of the Lake of Two Mountains.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No. 1)

name: Temiscamingue
location: At the head of Lake Temiscamingue in the County of Pontiac.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No. 1)

name: Whitworth
location: Lots 27, 28 and 29, Concession 12, Township of Whitworth, County of Temiscouata.
tribe_band: Amalecites of Isle Verte and Viger
remarks: Purchased by the Department of Indian Affairs, 31th March, 1877.

name: Cacouna
location: Lot No. 66, shown on the cadastral plan of the Village of Cacouna, County of Temiscouata.
tribe_band: Amalecites of Isle Verte and Viger
remarks: Purchased by the Department of Indian Affairs, 8th July, 1891.

name: Weymontachingue
location: On the north side of the St. Maurice River, opposite the mouth of the Manouan River, County of Champlain.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No. 1)

name: Coucoucache
location: On the north side of the St. Maurice River, opposite the mouth of the outlet from Lake Coucoucache, County of Champlain.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., Chap. 106. (See No. 1)

name: Escoumains
location: Near the mouth of the Escoumains River, Township of Escoumains, County of Saguenay.
remarks: Purchased in 1892 by the Department of Indian Affairs.
